messages:
sanjay: onboarding note — tried to pipx install our sample CLI wheel and then `import redwood` in a fresh venv -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood'

elena: ugh that pattern again. paste pipx output + pyproject please

sanjay: pipx log:
```
$ pipx install dist/serverless_cli-0.2.1-py3-none-any.whl
Installing into environment ... done.
ERROR: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood'
```
pyproject has `[tool.poetry] name = "serverless-cli"` but top-level package dir is `redwood/`

Tim_r: likely poetry used project name to build package root. poetry autodiscovery can miss dirs if packages not declared. try `packages = [{"include": "redwood"}]` under [tool.poetry] or rename dir to match name.

elena: also `MANIFEST.in` and `include` matter for sdist -> wheel differences. unzip the wheel: `unzip -l dist/*.whl` and check RECORD.

sanjay: did that — wheel contains `serverless_cli/__init__.py` and metadata, but zero redwood/ files. weird. building with `poetry build` from main checkout shows package in editable env only.

tim_r: this is classic: editable install reads local package dir, wheel uses package name mapping. Poetry by default includes packages matching project name if it finds a package with same name; otherwise it falls back to name-based layout. explicit packages mapping fixes it.

elena: another gotcha: extras and optional deps can be lost when exporting requirements for pipx or CI. if you rely on `extras = { ... }` make sure wheel metadata includes them or add a proper `pyproject` extras table. pipx install of a plain wheel won't pull extras unless bracket notation used.

sanjay: FYI mypy downstream flagged missing `py.typed` too. so typing/stubs not distributed which breaks strict typechecks.

tim_r: add `include = ["py.typed"]` or `package-data` to pyproject. For poetry: `packages = [{"include": "redwood"}]` and `include = ["redwood/**", "py.typed"]`. Then `poetry build` -> `unzip -l` to validate.

elena: quick smoke test CI idea: build wheel, create venv, `pip install --no-deps dist/*.whl`, `python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__name__)"` and fail build on non-zero. saves new hires time.

sanjay: workaround for now: pip install -e . or `pipx install --pip-args='-e .'` to get editable dev install. not ideal for releases.

build-bot: opened PR #456 by elena: add explicit packages, include py.typed, and add wheel smoke test to sampleapp CI. CI will run on push :github: :robot_face:

sanjay: thanks all — will retest after PR. learned to always check wheel contents before tagging a release :memo:
